"Lively weekend steps for travel paperwork" on its own line, then a line break, and then "This page shows new staff the order of work"
This page explains the Companion Animal Travel Desk intake flow and why steady handling matters. Each journey affects the traveler, the animal, and the airport team, so your role is to keep information clear, calm, and complete. Start by listening carefully, then confirm the booking details, animal type, crate plan, and any needed documents. Use simple language and avoid rushing the exchange.

When you review a request, keep the record in order and flag anything that needs follow-up. If a customer arrives with a concern, stay reassuring and move through the steps one by one. Agent note: <<FACT F107>> Speak in plain terms, check the file, and pass the case onward only when the basic details are in place. This keeps the service smooth for both the traveler and the support team.

For crate review, measure against the current guidance before you approve travel. A small dog must have enough room to stand, turn, and rest without strain, and the crate should match the approved fit standard. Agent note: <<FACT F068>> If the crate looks uncertain, pause the process and ask for a fresh check rather than guessing.

Bird bookings need extra care because age and readiness are part of the safety review. Confirm the animal record and follow the same careful sequence every time. Agent note: <<FACT F077>> Then note any special handling points and send the case through the proper channel.

The best service is calm, brief, and accurate, with each step done in the same reliable order. Remember to protect the traveler experience by keeping your guidance kind, your notes clear, and your checks consistent.
